source_refs.note: Topic 2.4.1.4 Nested and Chained Conditionals (PDF 43-44, printed 40-41). The syntax comments print 'conditionl'.

blocks.text: Sometimes, we need to check multiple conditions inside another condition. This is called nesting.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the printed syntax, if condition2: and the else: that belongs to it start at the same margin as if condition1:. For a nested if they must be indented inside if condition1: (four spaces), with their comments indented once more; only the last else: stays at the margin.
Example: If the weather is rainy and the temperature is below 15 degrees, we wear a raincoat. If it is only rainy, we take an umbrella. If the weather is not rainy, we just enjoy the day.
